Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and the wake-visual inspection skill, then inspect the current rollout evidence before touching the target policy. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and will not look for the omitted research shelf.

I’m using the wake-visual skill because the sampled evidence includes keyframe sheets. Its required sequence is now controlling the work: anchor images to observations and metrics, inspect the shared prewarm and rollout sheets, then write the diagnosis before editing the candidate.

The sampled current rollouts are four exact gain-1.7 successes, so there is no semantic failure among them. The most informative inherited counterexample is the separately tested 0.45 steering redistribution: it still captures, but degrades arrival, distance, crossflow, loads, energy, and score. I’ll compare that finite regression visually against the replicated 1.7 anchor, while treating the older domain-exit/instability reports only as outer safety boundaries.

The visual and diagnostic cross-check is decisive: the 0.45 redistribution does not balance the joints—it raises both peak angles, slows both mean velocity components, lengthens the route in time, and increases crossflow, force, moment, and effort. I’m recording that diagnosis and a single-axis hypothesis first; only afterward will I change the candidate.

The candidate now changes exactly one controller axis: `anterior_steering_fraction` from 0.40 to 0.35. I also added the durable negative lesson from the failed 0.45 redistribution. Next I’m running the required workspace checker and will repair any contract or schema failure it reports; I will not run CFD.

The first required check exposed a workspace-rendering defect before evaluating my edits: `README.md` contains the same “copied to guidance/” parent marker twice, so the checker finds two assigned parents. I’m inspecting the checker and marker context to determine the narrowest in-workspace repair, then I’ll rerun it.

The guidance check passes. The Julia contract command is blocked by the execution environment—`julia` is not on `PATH` (the login shell also emitted unrelated missing-SSH-directory setup errors). I’m checking for a workspace/host Julia binary and will rerun the exact lightweight contract check if one exists; meanwhile I’ll still run the independent boundary check.

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:11): tests `anterior_steering_fraction=0.35`, preserving all other anchor parameters.
